metadata.title: Current computer sales and package financials

quarter_reasons: Apple business bundles and Tandy CP/M alternatives modestly displace demand; IBM has no qualified disk OS.
Artemis qualification and native application availability constrain adoption; C source portability is not binary compatibility.
Peripheral adapters and developer ports support demand, offset by selective enterprise purchasing.
Native applications mature; independent OEM agreements remain qualification prospects, not automatic orders.
CP/M/TUI installed base and documented interfaces sustain demand; no CP/M-86 competitor exists.
Network launch and BPI pilots increase interest; portable CP/M competitors limit workstation growth.
Recession and cautious dealer inventory offset conditional PRO availability; storage and recovery gates constrain server uptake.
Team Edition pilots and developer interest support a modest spike; four-seat teams and 5 MB storage limit initial scope.
IBM independent disk-OS launch assumed March 1982; recession and buyer waiting constrain growth.
IBM business-channel credibility offsets cheaper Logix RAM and platform maturity; 286 availability starts port feasibility only.
DRI 68k prototype work and third-party drivers support confidence; no production 68k AIONix or x86 AIONix revenue assumed.
Late-year recovery, qualified compatibility and developer references support a forecast demand spike; no unqualified process savings.
policy.method: Accepted 1980 factors are already incorporated in sales_model_inputs.json and are not applied again. 1981–82 quarterly run rates are relative to reassessed December 1980, replacing 4% compounded monthly growth. Existing balanced prices are held; no second price-elasticity or marketing bonus. Bounds are judgement scenarios, not statistical intervals.
premises: CP/M-86 does not exist; DRI prioritizes CP/M-80/TUI and AIONix/PRO.
Adam owns 30% of independent DRI; IBM sees a strategic conflict with competitor Logix.
Paterson does not create QDOS; IBM commissions its own alternative disk OS, with qualification risk.
DRI non-ERA port rights activate in 1982; 68k requires suitable MMU/system design; 286 enables feasibility, not an immediate release.
ERAv1 remains 3 um. June 1982 repaired 3 um RAM costs remain the volume cost basis through year-end; 2 um pilot savings await repeatable-production approval.
Adam foresees demand peaks, not engineering success: reserve 5% commercial headroom, retain OEE, one-down redundancy and qualification gates.
policy.team_scope: Small four-developer teams and pilots; existing 5 MB server constrains repositories. No large-storage product or enterprise-scale deployment assumed. Client and server purchases are contained in computer totals, not added again.
policy.external_revenue_boundary: No external OEM, 68k/x86 AIONix port or unpriced storage revenue; independent third-party sales are not Logix receipts.

financial_policy.scope: Computer baskets only. Standalone Team Edition, BPI, cards, upgrades and Academy revenue remain separate in ROI. Bundle components appear once; their constituent editions are not additional sales.
financial_policy.retail_spend: Quantity × dated retail_price_usd for every weighted basket offer.
financial_policy.after_channel_fees: Quantity × dated revenue_after_fee_usd, already net of the modeled fee.
financial_policy.recurring_cost: Quantity × dated manufacturing_cost_usd; includes the recurring contents and services defined in retail pricing.
financial_policy.contribution: After channel fees minus recurring cost, before corporate development, marketing, capital/depreciation and tax.
financial_policy.timing: Use June snapshot from June onward, prior-year snapshot January–May. First available snapshot is a labelled proxy for offers introduced after the prior snapshot. June snapshots proxy the whole month.
financial_policy.rounding: Round each weighted offer line to cents, then sum lines, months, quarters and years. Contribution is net receipts minus recurring cost in integer cents.
financial_policy.demand: Accepted central demand unchanged. Conservative/strong scale each product count by 0.8/1.2 once; these are scenario bounds, not separate historical versions.
